tldr: Midday batch (Sep 5): OpenAI is under scrutiny after Fortune tracked post-launch edits to GPT-6 Astra's benchmark post — the coding score was nudged up 57.7 to 57.9% and some rival comparisons down, with Stanford researchers flagging 'benchmaxxing' and the system card thin on eval method. Google patched CVE-2026-85046, an already-exploited Chrome zero-day (V8 type-confusion, CVSS 8.8) now on CISA's KEV list — worth watching beyond browsers since Chromium is the substrate under agent tooling. Nous Research teased an open-source-harness announcement ('wait till they learn'), days after Teknium's Hermes Agent self-refactor shed 375K lines, and the community logged Qwen3.8-Flash-Next running fully on-device on a phone CPU.

articles.summary: Post-launch edits to Astra's Sep 3 benchmark post: coding up 57.7 to 57.9%, some rival comparisons down — Stanford researchers flag 'benchmaxxing'.

articles.title: Google patches actively exploited Chrome zero-day (CVE-2026-85046)
articles.summary: V8 type-confusion (CVSS 8.8) already exploited in the wild and on CISA's KEV list; Chromium underpins agent browsers — update to 152.0.7977.82+.

articles.title: Nous Research teases open-source harnesses for Hermes Agent
articles.summary: Sep 5 tease: 'wait till they learn about open source harnesses' — hot on Teknium's 375K-line Hermes self-refactor; announcement expected within days.

articles.title: Qwen3.8-Flash-Next runs fully local on a phone CPU
articles.summary: Xiaomi 14T Pro runs Flash-Next fully on-device (IQ3_XXS via BigMoeOnEdge) — another efficiency datapoint for the MoE on constrained hardware.
